  - _The correction_ (2.4, as follow-ups 1, 3, 4 and 6–9 rebuilt it; `ebm::corrected`,
    `ZonalSearch`, `search`, `next_search_step`, `defect_slope`, `g2_start`, `second_run`,
    `kept_run`):
    - the fit labels a fold whenever its final probe misses T\* by more than 0.1 K (`FOLD_MISS_K`),
      converged or not, a converged final probe replacing its side's last candidate; at a
      snowball-class fold (`SNOWBALL_FOLD_ICE_SHARE`) the candidate whose ice share lies nearer
      `ice_fraction()` is taken (`nearer_side`); the fit records its candidates;
    - the zonal search Z(T\*) on the fit's zonal model (band-mean sea shares, ground, ocean and
      sunlight, `Sunlight::band_means`), each run under the search's stop, 0.01 K
      (`SEARCH_CONVERGENCE_K`), recording whether it met the climate's stop (0.1 K) and the
      search's: Z₀ at the fit's u from its zonal steady state; Z₁ by the two-sided steady slope at
      u₀ ± 0.05 from the nearest run that met the climate's stop; from Z₂ the secant on the latest
      two runs that met the search's stop, held inside them where they straddle the target and
      otherwise to four times their step (`SECANT_STEP_CAP`), started from their secant predictor
      of end states and return temperatures, linear in u (follow-up 7 §1); halfway to an
      unconverged latest run from the nearest converged one; until a run that met the search's stop
      lies within 0.01 K, or six runs (`SEARCH_RUNS`); its answer the nearest run that met the
      climate's stop;
    - on the zonal grid the answer is the climate; elsewhere G1, a measurement of d and of G2's
      start (follow-up 8 §1), at the answer's u from its end state broadcast, under `G1_STOP`: the
      climate's stop, or its probe stop where that comes first (`ebm::probe_end`, as follow-up 9
      §1 amends it): after at least four fresh orbits since its start or its last jump that stood
      (`PROBE_FRESH_ORBITS`; a reject restores the count and the mean's changes, `MeanTrail`), at the first
      orbit where the surface mean's own last two ratios ρ_n = δ_n ÷ δ_n−1 and ρ_n−1 each lie in
      (0, 1) and agree within 0.05 (`PROBE_AGREEMENT`), and its remainder R̄ = |δ_n| r\* ÷ (1 − r\*)
      is at most 0.05 K (`PROBE_STOP_K`), r\* = max(the stop's own ratio, ρ_n) (`stop_ratio`, which
      `settled_after` reads too), δ_n the surface mean's change over the orbit; its probe records
      ρ_n, ρ_n−1, r\*, R̄ and T̂ = T̄_n + δ_n r\* ÷ (1 − r\*) at the orbit it ended, by either stop
      (`MeanProbe`; at the climate's stop `settled_probe`, ρ_n read only where it lies in (0, 1));
    - G2 always runs (`second_run`), at u_Z − d ÷ S_Z (d = T̂ − T̄_Z, S_Z the secant of the search's
      two runs nearest T\* that met its stop and lie 0.1 K or more apart, `DEFECT_PAIR_SPREAD_K`,
      else the steady slope), held to the bracket, started from G1's end plus the broadcast zonal
      predictor's change over that pair, and likewise its return temperatures (G1's end alone
      without a pair), under the climate's stop; or run A where G1 reached its last orbit under
      neither stop, having measured no d, or the search has no answer. G2 is kept where it
      converged, G1 where only it met the climate's stop, the nearer where neither did
      (`kept_run`); follow-up 4's early end at a G1 within 0.1 K (`CORRECTION_TOLERANCE_K`) is
      gone. Every run's u, surface mean, orbits, jumps, rejects, start (steady, continued or
      predicted) and both flags, G1's probe, d, S_Z and its pair and G2's start mean are recorded
      (`MeanCorrection::{Zonal, Searched}`, G2 no longer optional), and the slow coarse-pass test
      prints them;
    - the spin-up's extrapolation (follow-ups 4, 6 and 7; `Extrapolation`): after an orbit whose
      stop fails on its remainder, m r ÷ (1 − r) at least the bound with r in (0.3, 0.97)
      (`JUMP_RATIO_RANGE`), every point's end state and stored annual mean shift by the orbit's
      annual change times r ÷ (1 − r), at most once every two orbits (`JUMP_SPACING_ORBITS`) and
      only where two more orbits fit; a first fresh move larger than the move before the jump
      rejects it, restoring the state, the means and the return temperatures to the bit; after a
      reject a jump needs two successive ratios within 0.05 (`JUMP_AGREEMENT`); at most two rejects
      a run (`MAX_REJECTS`); after a jump that stood, the stop's remainder reads r\* = max(r, the
      ratio of the run's last jump) (`settled_after`); a run without jumps is unchanged to the bit;
    - the stop: the move under the bound, the moves shrinking and their extrapolated remainder
      under it, at least 3 orbits (`MIN_ORBITS`), at most 40; the transport's pressure factor falls
      linearly to zero below 0.2 bar (`transport::pressure_factor`), bit for bit at and above it.

  - _Choices the ruling did not state_:
    - nitrogen's collision factor in τ_d at the model's own equilibrium with its sunlight at T\*,
      σT_eq⁴ = (1 − α(T\*)) F ÷ 4 + F_int (256.4 K on Earth against plan 14's 255.1 K, 1% in
      nitrogen's term), since the inputs carry no equilibrium temperature;
    - the vapour cap's criterion: water among a surface liquid's components (pure, or an aqueous
      solution's), a brine's water as much a reservoir as a fresh sea's (follow-up 5 §4); its
      water activity, p_w = a_w `h_w` p_sat, is P14.T52's;
    - the sea's liquid is `liquids()`'s first, the one the relief step floods; `Freezing::Never`'s
      reference temperature is plan 14's mean; d̄ counts every liquid's flooded cells, as the sea
      shares do;
    - the Ekman cells' return temperatures are the state's own in the steady state and a run's
      first orbit (`Returning::Own`), then each band's previous-orbit coldest month
      (`Returning::Coldest`, boxed per band), read for T_R at the template's first node at its
      Earth share of the way from the edge to the pole (`wind::return_latitude_deg`) and for
      T_sub; the equator's edge reads the northern hemisphere's; an edge's sea temperature is the
      mean of its two bands'; the Ekman mass flux's sea share is the edge's points' mean;
    - K_o takes no factor of the body's radius: the conductance is per R² as the model's Laplacian
      is (low confidence either way);
    - a run whose state is no longer finite mid-orbit leaves the Ekman gains at zero (a band's h
      not finite), so the orbit ends and the run stops unconverged rather than panicking;
    - a move of exactly nothing stops a run; every u of a run is held to the fit's bracket (the
      slope's two steady probes are not runs); where no zonal run's mean is finite, G1 is run A;
    - test 5's reference is Setzmann and Wagner's Table 39 at 100 K over the WebBook's IAPWS-95 at
      275 K (0.3550), not NIST's ratio at the registry's 100.7 K (0.1% in ρ c_p, inside the 2%);
    - the ocean record holds each step's starting-state fluxes, which the step applies implicitly,
      so batch 2's Q_O will not close exactly on the energy the model moved; a one-month year
      records its steady state's fluxes;
    - the test-only `ebm::solve_continued`, `solve_at_fit` and `EnergyBalance::ekman_at` make the
      relief effect's sea-level run, the extrapolation's and the models' comparisons and the
      aquaplanet's ψ print;
    - the test set-up's sea floor `SYNTHETIC_SEA_DEPTH_M` is the reference Earth's mean depth,
      1.335 × 10¹⁸ m³ over 0.7095 of 510.082 × 10¹² m², 3,689 m (§2.5).

    `Circulation::share`).
    - As ruled: beyond the centre in its own hemisphere the Gaussian's width is σ_x max(0, 1 − |c|

      `Circulation::share`.

  - _The sea's evaporation_ (§3.2; `evaporation::year_rates_kg_m2_s`, `OpenMonth`, `energy_w_m2`,
    `Moisture::saturation_specific_humidity`).
    - As ruled, over each sea cell's open months.
    - `Q_O` is the kept run's `OceanRecord` convergence over the point's sea share, zero at a point
      with no sea (`per_sea_area`), carried in `OwnRecords::ocean_w_m2`.
    - G is the storage as built, with batch 1's r_l.
    - A one-month year takes `rate_kg_m2_s` on β `S_abs` + `Q_O` to the bit, and is as built to the
      bit where no ocean heat reaches it (tested).
  - _Choices the ruling did not state_:
    - ⟨·⟩ is the open months' share-weighted mean normalised by their shares, Σ s x ÷ Σ s. The
      year's amount Σ s E is the same under the unnormalised reading.
    - `q_s` is the saturation specific humidity at the surface pressure, its vapour pressure capped
      at that pressure as `Moisture::specific_humidity` caps it (`q_s` 1 where the liquid boils).
      `specific_humidity` is now `humidity_at(t, RELATIVE_HUMIDITY)`, the same arithmetic to the
      bit. Where no open month holds any vapour (⟨`q_s`⟩ zero), the aerodynamic part is spread
      evenly.
    - The one-month year reads no saturation.
    - §3.5 2's "with no storage and a constant temperature every open month is equal" and "`Q_O` = 0
      and G = 0 give PT's rate in every month" hold as written only where the months' forcing is
      uniform: the aerodynamic part is spread by `q_s`, not by the energy. Both are built as one
      test on uniform months (constant coefficient, energy and saturation, with and without a frozen
      month): every open month equal to the bit, and PT's rate to 10⁻¹². With a varying energy
      the months differ from PT's month by month, and their year is PT's amount (the year test).
    - The ruled Earth's test asserts the blocking bounds, DJF ÷ JJA ≤ 7.5 and JJA ÷ DJF ≥ 0.35. It
      prints "REPORT to main" between them and the ruled 6 and 0.45. Neither printed on this tree.
    - The observed-temperature data follow the ruling's prototype, its `obs_weighting.py` "zonal"
      variant, exactly:
      - cos φ weights of the T62 rows;
      - the 2.5° grid's surface height at the nearest row and column (Python's ties to even);
      - Γ 5.818 K km⁻¹, against the reference Earth's own 5.817883, which the test checks to
        5 × 10⁻⁷ K m⁻¹.
    - The test weights its annual mean by the calendar months' days (February 28.25), as the
      prototype does, and its seasons by equal months.
    - The latent transport it prints is the budget's E − P integrated from the south pole.
    - From the review:
      - A world locked 1:1 has no summer side: `Circulation::share` keeps Siler et al.'s width
        there by construction (an edge at no finite sine), so that §3.1's "unchanged" holds
        wherever a locked world's greatest h lies, not only at its substellar band. This is tested
        about off-pole centres.
      - The evaporation precomputes each point's energy A once a run (`Evaporation::energy_w_m2`)
        rather than cloning the ocean table: the same arithmetic.
    - The printed "observed" brackets are GPCP less NCEP R1's evaporation scaled by 0.944 to close
      its global budget on GPCP's (decision-r09-t13e-revision §1.2), not NCEP's own P − E (−0.52 at
      40–60° N). The labels say so.

      +1.43.
    - The sea's DJF ÷ JJA is the band-solid-angle window of `e_b`, as T13.j's 8.9 was measured. The
      same weighted by each band's sea, as the stand-ins weight it, is printed beside it: 4.46.

      band would need it added.

  - _Files and items._ In the surface crate, `synth/craters.rs`: `CraterProfile::filleted` and its
    private `height_and_slope`, with one private field, `cone_kept`, the cone's kept share p (`None`
    where the fillet stops short of the cone); and the documentation of the module's "# The profile"
    and "# The closed forms", of `CraterProfile`, `filleted` and `compensation`.
    `synth/craters/rims.rs`' "# The sharpening" and `synth/craters/bound.rs`' "# One crater's
    shares" and `fillet_change` changed in their documentation alone. Tests in
    `synth/craters/tests.rs`, `synth/craters/rims/tests.rs` and the sim's `steps/craters/tests.rs`.
    - No public signature changed and no item or panic was added. `CraterProfile::compensation`
      keeps its signature, and its amplitude c is now the term's height at the rim, x = 1, where it
      was its height at the centre: its documentation says so.
    - `RimSharpening`, `CoarseRims::coarse_profile`, `sharpening_moment_m4`, `increase_m4` and the
      sim's `each_lift` call `filleted` and are unchanged, as are `breakpoints`, `square_moment` and
      `rims::difference_moments`: the breakpoints already bracket [0, x₀], `c_p` and the span, and
      every piece stays one polynomial of degree at most 4.
  - _The construction, as the brief's §2.3 has it._ On the span [x₀, x₁] = [1 − w, 1 + w] the
    profile is the cubic Hermite plus c (1 − u²)², u = (x − 1) ÷ w, with c = −15 Δ ÷ (32 w); outside
    it, the fresh shape, to the bit. Where x₀ < `c_p` it is the floor, −d₀, for x ≤ x₀ (the centre
    itself where x₀ is 0), the Hermite from (−d₀, 0) at x₀, and the cone at p = x₀ ÷ `c_p` of its
    relief P on [0, `c_p`]; there Δ = ∫ H + (−d₀) x₀² + p P `c_p`² ÷ 3 less the fresh moment over
    [0, x₁]. The leans:
    - The floor for x ≤ x₀ is −d₀ itself: the coneless shape is the floor there, since the cone's
      base is never wider than the floor (`crater_shape` takes the lesser).
      `a_central_cone_s_base_lies_within_its_floor` holds it from 0.5 to 100 `D_t` on the five test
      contracts; `craters/shape.rs` is unchanged.
    - The fade is x₀ < `c_p`, strictly. At x₀ = `c_p` the profile takes the as-built form, where p
      would be 1 and the two forms agree.
    - The Hermite and the compensation take the open span, x₀ < x < x₁, so x₀ and x₁ themselves are
      the fresh shape's bits (or the floor's and the faded cone's); the term is zero with a zero
      slope at both ends.
    - Δ is summed left to right as written, in `f64`, with no transcendental; p is one division.

    abstracts of Riedel et al. 2020 and Talkington et al. 2022): booked as a first-order rate shared
    with obliteration, mostly obliteration at the coarse sizes' slopes, the survivors would be
    fresher (E[g²] 0.36–0.51 at η 2.4–2.8, main's estimate, against the uniform reading's 0.2638; η
    is the production's local cumulative slope, N(>D) ∝ D^−η, which sets Minton et al.'s eqs. 27–28
    split, read from the code's Neukum polynomial, addendum 5, E1.6), so the largest, oldest craters
    may be over-worn; the superposition's missing overprinting may offset it. For T7.j's
    re-validation, with a measured depth distribution of degraded highland complex craters, none
    read.

  - _The law, as the brief's §2.4 has it._ g = (b ÷ (K ÷ R² + b))², b = `DEGRADATION_B`, with K ÷ R²
    = `num::max`(κt ÷ R², `K_v` q) and κt ÷ R² = ½ (L ÷ R)² as built, so that a crater whose
    diffusion is the larger keeps its g, its profile and its heights to the bit. The leans:
    - _`OctaveWear`, a public type the brief does not name._ It holds T7.b's and T12.d's window rule
      (τ and `N_w` from `N_S`, P, S and the system's age, by the expressions both used) and q's rate
      P ÷ (S `N_S`), so the synthesis, the coarse pass and the maturity mix read one window and one
      law; and it makes the closed form public, which the sim's basin-share test reads at the coarse
      octaves.
    - _q from the age_ (the lane's lean): `CraterWear::of_age(age, &octave)` is
      `diffusion_length(age)` and q = N(t) × P ÷ (S `N_S`), N(t) = `lunar_chronology(age, A)`, zero
      where P or `N_S` is zero; so q is the draw share u through `chronology_age` (tested).
    - `CraterWear::new` refuses a diffusion or share that is not finite and non-negative, and
      accepts q above 1 (a crater past its window, which the maturity helper's bisection reaches);
      `relief_factor` now refuses a bad rim radius alone, the wear carrying the rest.
    - _The basin-share term at the nodes._ The test sums Σ_k `e_k` ⟨`E_k`[g²](D) ∫F(`w₂`)² dA⟩_k,
      the mean over each coarse octave's eight Gauss–Legendre diameter nodes of the node's
      closed-form E[g²] times its ∫F(`w₂`)² dA, where the brief wrote `E_k`[g²] ⟨∫F(`w₂`)² dA⟩_k.
      The two agree on the Moon, whose every coarse octave keeps E[g²] 0.2638 at every diameter, and
      the node form is the exact expectation where E[g²] varies with D (Mars, Ceres). The test also
      holds plan 14's `Relief::of` basin share for the reference Moon within 10 m of 2,050 m (2,045
      m, at its gravity of 1.6243 m s⁻²).
    - `for_body` still reads the surface's density before its loop, so that a surface older than its
      system is refused on a body of no octave too, as its documentation says.
    - _The maturity helper_ (the lane's lean): the test helper `immature_rims_per_km2`, the closed
      form of the synthesis's rim deficit compared with Grier et al.'s count, takes the same law,
      each diameter's octave from `CraterOctaves::new`, and prints the ruling's κ-only figures
      beside it, labelled.
  - _The closed form, as the lane designed it._ With c = `K_v` P ÷ (S `N_S`), the closure's K ÷ R²
    is c N(t). N is convex in t with N(0) = 0, so α t − c N(t) changes sign at most once, at t\*: 0
    where α ≤ c N′(0), τ where α τ ≥ c `N_w`, else a bisection of 64 halvings. κ's part on [0, t\*]
    is T7.b's (the linear term closed, the exponential's eight panels of eight-point
    Gauss–Legendre), to the bit as built where t\* = τ; the closure's is closed in N, (b ÷ 3c)
    [(b ÷ (c N\* + b))³ − (b ÷ (c `N_w` + b))³], written as the span times (1 + y\*)⁻³ (1 −
    e^(−3d)) ÷ 3δ through `exp_m1` and `ln_1p`, which tends to the span as c falls to zero.
  - _Constants._ `K_v` = 0.17, Minton et al. 2019's `K_v,1` at γ = 2 (eq. 7, p. 15; Fig. 5, p. 16;

    built. Not modelled, and labelled: fluvial and aeolian infill, viscous relaxation, mare or melt

- **Deviations in T6.c, as built** (2026-10-22; lane r09-valleys, from `e1a44211`; built to
  decision-r09-t14-choices F2 with its T14.c and T14.d follow-ups, decision-r09-t14-mars-ceiling §2
  and §5, and main's rulings of 2026-10-22 on the payload, the size test and the tributaries).
  - _Trunks alone (main's ruling, option A)._ On a world dry now the epoch's level cut is the coarse
    level: `deepest_level` is L, `ChannelNetwork::tributary` heads no segment below a dry-now cell,
    and the closed forms carry the trunk's one term. The ruled tributary incision, the cell's at
    the same K t in the short-time regime, (`r_t` `A_t`)^m `S_t` ÷ (r̄ A)^m S, is identically 1 on
    T6.b's tributary profiles: `S_t` = `k_s` (r̄ ÷ `r_t`)^θ `A_t`^−θ and m = θ give
    (`r_t` `A_t`)^θ `S_t` = r̄^θ `k_s` = (r̄ A)^θ S, and it exceeds 1 only where the 10⁻⁵ minimum slope
    binds, so it cuts no level. The alternative measured, the tributaries T6.b's inherited valley
    top keeps below the top (which is the epoch's headward knickpoint reach: the steady-state rise
    from a key point to its join at most the trunk's incision, Ψ = K t r̄^m = d ÷ `k_s`, median
    1.99 m^0.1, median two levels, up to T6.b's own cut at L + 4), gave the reference Mars 0.177
    km⁻¹ of valleys over the eroded Lid (15 times Hynek et al.'s 0.0115), (A2) 6.14 m and (B)'s p99
    304 m, 3.3 times its bound, each finer level adding about 1.0 m of layer (closed forms on the
    final records; the lane's scratch measurement). A depth cut on the short-time incision at the
    construction's slope, I_t = d (`A_t` ÷ A)^0.45, needs an unsourced figure and was not built.
  - _The valley._ `EpochValley::of` (public, `synth/channels/incision.rs`): G = min(T6.b's groove
    min(max(`valley_depth`, `d_bf`), `G_max`), the coded incision), with no floor at the bankfull
    depth, so a valley the epoch cut less deep than its channel is as shallow as its incision; the
    floor the bankfull channel; each wall W = min(5 G, T6.b's ½-cell wall) (`WALL_RUN_PER_DEPTH`,
    moved here from the sim's branch). The cap keeps each groove inside the 5 × 5 search's reach and
    binds only where G exceeds a tenth of the cell (3.8 km on the reference Mars); the steepest wall
    is then 1.5 G ÷ W ≤ 0.6 by T6.b's cap, and 0.3 elsewhere. `epoch_valley(cell, body)` reads it
    from a record; the trunk's `below_top` is G. A dry-now cell with channels but no runoff of its
    own (a cell renewed after part of the epoch) takes `valley_depth` at its own `k_s`, where T6.b's
    would give no valley. The closed forms take a dry-now cell's one level whole: its variance and
    structure function without `WHOLE_VARIANCE_SHARE` (whose 0.52 is the levels'
    anticorrelation): on the epoch Mars-like world the realised over the closed form was 1.2–2.7 at
    0.52, within T6.b's factor of two at 1.
  - _The code._ `LogIncision`, one byte after `catchment_runoff` (the sea floor's byte stays last):
    0 `NONE`, no epoch (worlds wet now or never wet: T6.b as built); 1 `UNCUT`, a world dry now's
    cell the epoch did not cut (a renewed province, inside a waiting crater's rim, a bound, an
    incision under about 0.49 m); c ≥ 2, 0.5 m × 2^((c − 2) ÷ 16), 4.4% steps to 28.8 km, above the
    reference Mars's 22.5 km construction (main accepted 0.25 m to 14 km; the start moved to 0.5 m
    for that range and was reported to main). An incision past the last code takes it, so that no
    world's pass is refused: the sim's edifice cap, `TALLEST_EDIFICE_RELIEF` × (3.71 ÷ g), can pass
    28.8 km below about 2.8 m s⁻², and a synthesised valley, at most a fifth of a cell deep, never
    reads past the code (the review's must-fix). `BuildFieldError::IncisionWithoutAir` refuses any
    other code than `NONE` on an airless body, as its runoffs are. A field mixing `NONE` with epoch
    codes is not refused (the coarse pass makes none; deferred).
    The record is 26 bytes; `SURFACE_PAYLOAD_FORMAT` stays 1 and `GENERATOR_VERSION` 23 (main: the
    layout freezes at the gate, and the sea-floor and runoff bytes set the precedent; the format's
    documentation now says so); `wire/`'s,
    `worker/`'s and the Mars-like world's goldens re-blessed at 23. The Earth-like payload is
    15,141,470 bytes (`payloads.golden`), and the size test is bound at R03's 15 MiB (Risks, "Field
    size"). The client's `sessionContacts.test.ts` reads the 26-byte stride.
  - _The quantiser and the rims._ `quantise::synthesis_record` takes the inputs: `UNCUT` or the
    incision on a world dry now (`Branch::DryNow`), `NONE` otherwise. `CellState::channel_incision`
    is zero inside a waiting crater's rim (1,216 of the reference Mars's 98,304 cells), whose ground
    formed after the epoch, so no valley is drawn there under a late crater; the solver's own
    `DryNow::incision_m` is unchanged, and (A1) reads it.
  - _The closure._ `dry_now_lowering_m` is min(d, `MEAN_TRUNK_LENGTH` G (`w_bf` + W) ÷ w) for the
    valley the synthesis draws (`drawn_valley`, through `EpochValley::of`), and zero inside a
    waiting rim (`DryNow::{young, valley_m}`). The branch runs before the final routing, so it reads
    the coded incision but the construction's `k_s` on the solve's last routing, the epoch's runoff
    and the solve's drainage, where the synthesis reads the final field's codes. On the reference
    Mars the closed form on the final codes gives (A2) 2.068 m against the closure's 1.961 m, the
    per-cell ratio within −5% and +3% at p10 and p90, and 14 cells draw a valley on one side alone
    (the final routing moving a flow or a catchment). On the Mars-like world the realised first
    level's void is 1.19 times the closure's (its trunks run 1.12 cells against
    `MEAN_TRUNK_LENGTH`'s 1.0, R09.T6.b's, and each groove's ends add their caps), so its upland
    stands about a fifth of a cell's lowering above its construction.
  - _`has_channels` and the trunks._ `has_channels` needs a catchment runoff above `NONE` (T14.d
    follow-up C), and `ChannelNetwork::trunk` heads no trunk where no water reaches a cell, on every
    world. No Earth-like golden moved, so the wet-now synthesis is T6.b's to the bit wherever every
    channelled cell's catchment sheds runoff, as on the Earth-like world; on a generated world wet
    now a hyperarid cell's catchment under 0.1 mm a⁻¹ loses its zero-depth trunk, a join target
    the less for its neighbours' tributaries (ruled, and pinned by no golden).
  - _The test worlds._ The Mars-like world has an epoch, `FieldBuilder::epoch(Ψ)` with Ψ 2.0
    m^0.1, the reference Mars's median d ÷ `k_s`: each routed dry cell with a channel was cut Ψ
    `k_s` deep, the short-time regime's K t (r̄ A)^m S. `testing::mars_like_without_its_epoch` keeps
    T6.b's steady state on a dry world for T6.b's own tests, whose `mars()` it now is. The height
    golden's "with channels" cells take a dry world's epoch-valley cells. The panics tests' flowing
    field has 610 Pa and a catchment runoff, since a cell no water reaches heads no trunk.
  - _The WebAssembly determinism review_ (the review's determinism auditor, read-only, on the
    uncommitted tree): no new tag or draw (key points stay keyed by cell on `surface.channel`, so
    skipping tributaries shifts no other draw); every new min and max is `num`'s, signed zeros and

  - _T14.a_ (`d29a0fc9`).
    - Barnes, Lehman and Mulla 2014's improved Priority-Flood (a FIFO pit queue) runs from the sea
      at ℓ and the terminal bodies' pits. A newly closed cell's parent is the cell that closed it
      (the lane's derivation from their Alg. 2), so flats drain in pop order, where Design note 9
      reads "ties by (elevation, cell index)".
    - A receiver is one strictly lower edge neighbour on the filled surface, in proportion to the
      drop per metre, from instance 0; with none, the parent. The slope correction S_r ÷ ‖∇W‖
      (Tzathas et al. §4.3, read from the rendered page) is held at 1 or below, since unequal
      cube-sphere links push it a little above; a receiver whose drops underflow falls back to the
      parent. Since the review the draw is an integer threshold, one `stream.mark()` word picked by
      `Mark::pick_weighted`: the same decision as u < p up to a rounding tie, so no figure moved.
    - Barnes, Callaghan and Wickert 2020's hierarchy is built as the terrain's merge tree (the
      lane's equivalent construction). In their 2021 Fill–Spill–Merge a sea-linked tree spills
      through its oceanlink, latest-linked first; a merge activates whenever both children are full;
      a depression no water fills is a terminal playa; a three-way saddle merges land first.
    - Volume (Q2) and Balance (Q3) take whole cells in fill order by the half-cell rule. **The level
      is the ground of the first cell not taken**, where Q3 reads the last cell's filled level:
      under the millimetre codes that keeps the last cell flooded and one-cell lakes real (accepted
      by main). Water bodies are found once a level, on its construction (matching Q1's fixed
      partition).
  - _T14.b_ (`fc121acb`; the start and receivers in `320fe222`; the uplift and threshold in
    `7347836a`; the remap's frame in `a8a25ee0`).
    - K = K⊕ (g ÷ g⊕)(ρ_f ÷ 1,000 kg m⁻³) B, g⊕ the pass's `EARTH_GRAVITY` (GM⊕ ÷ (6,371 km)²), ρ_f
      the main liquid's palette entry on a world wet now and the epoch liquid's triple-point density
      on one dry now (999.793 kg m⁻³ for water; Q6a). B: rock under water 1; crater-saturated
      regolith under water 10 (Barnhart, Howard and Moore 2009); ice under CH4, C2H6 or
      `ch4_c2h6_n2` 8 (Collins 2005; Litwin et al. 2012); other pairs 1, "not modelled" (closed set,
      for the composition audit); a saturated pair with no row takes its bedrock row, a labelled
      lower bound (T14.b follow-up (b)). Saturation is the lane's criterion, N_e = n₁ₖₘ (C(S) −
      C(min(E, S))) ÷ C(S) ≥ 0.018 km⁻², per crust on Province cells (mars-ceiling §2.1).
    - Measured K: Earth 6.2814 × 10⁻⁶ (−0.30%), Mars 2.3910 × 10⁻⁵ (−0.37%; N_e 2.80 times
      saturation), Titan 3.1112 × 10⁻⁶ (+0.36%). The reference Mars's K r^0.45 t = 1.866 m^0.1, 1.8%
      under 1.9 at GM ÷ R² = 3.7279 m s⁻² (follow-up (a)).
    - The solver: eqs. 8–9 over a preorder with a path array, D by binary search on τ; zero-A_eq
      cells keep z0; no deposition without uplift, z = min(…, z0). On the wet-now steady state alone
      a link rises at most s_c δ, s_c = `DEBRIS_FLOW_SLOPE`, 0.1 (T14.c follow-up §2). The
      ridge-to-sea profile is within 0.066% of its closed form for x ≤ 0.9 L, bit-equal below s_c,
      its last 5.9 km at s_c (follow-up 2 §5).
    - The multigrid: a parent is sea where half its solid angle is and its ground is at most ℓ;
      water bodies, basins and base levels once a level; after the six iterations, a final refit and
      re-solve. **A finer level starts from the correction upsample** (T14.b follow-up §3), its z0
      plus the jittered interpolant of the coarser z − z0 (instance 1). The finest level's last
      residuals for the three starts, the first build's (the interpolant of the coarser z), the
      construction and the correction: smooth 92.45, 82.40 and 82.18 m; rough 38.61, 14.70 and 30.08
      m; Mars 32.69, 22.51 and 23.32 m. The correction start is lowest only on the smooth world, and
      the construction start on the rough world and Mars. The rule takes the construction start only
      if it beats the correction on both synthetic worlds, so the correction stays (T14.b follow-up
      §3; T14.c follow-up §6's "it wins on two worlds out of three" reads the figures wrongly, to
      the same outcome).
    - The uplift (wet now) is Q1 as written: u(i) = λ_{b(i)} max(0, z0 − ℓ_b), each cell's own
      construction basin's λ in the path integral (T14.c follow-up §1), refitted additively, λ_b ←
      max(0, λ_b + ½ Σ_b Ω (z0 − s) ÷ S_b), S_b the basin's own sensitivity (follow-up 2 §1).
      Receivers are sticky on a world wet now from each level's third iteration (follow-up 2 §3);
      dry now keeps fresh receivers and no threshold.
    - The residual is not monotone over the levels, so the test is the fall within each, the last
      below half the first (T14.b follow-up §5; follow-up 2 §3). On the level-6 synthetic worlds by
      level: smooth 81.8, 71.3, 92.4 m; rough 67.4, 92.5, 38.6 m; also under one global λ and with
      no uplift.
  - _T14.c_ (`a6c551b4`, landed, was `0f42b78a`; `320fe222`).
    - `WetEpoch` gains `liquid` and `runoff_m_per_year` (Q6a); a negative runoff, or a liquid with
      no registry phase columns, is refused. The reference Mars's epoch is 2.2 × 10⁵ yr at 0.1 m a⁻¹
      of water (it was 10⁶ yr, no runoff); the reference Earth's runoff 0.29 is unread.
    - `province_surface_age` (mars-ceiling §2.1), within [0, S]: the reference Mars 0, the others S;
      `from_record` 0 until plan 14's `GlobalFigures::volcanic_surface_age`, which the tripwire
      names (decision-r09-t14-mars-ceiling §2.1).
    - Never wet, or no older than the epoch's end: nothing, every cell `Terminal`, `routed` unset
      (Q4; T14.d follow-up C).
    - Dry now: t = `effective_flow` × min(1, (S − end) ÷ (start − end)) (Q4); the epoch's runoff
      everywhere; the paleo-inventory by Fill–Spill–Merge at its liquid's density, its bodies bounds
      (Q2); every cell solved, waiting craters' included (Q4, labelled "a crater formed inside the
      epoch erodes for the whole t"). A cell whose exposure σ_c (S_p on Province cells) is under the
      global share takes its transient at `effective_flow` × σ_c, z0 to the bit at 0. The lowering
      written is min(d, d (w_bf + 5d) ÷ w), w_bf T6.b's `bankfull_width` at the epoch's
      channel-forming discharge and 5 the walls' run per depth, `WALL_RUN_PER_DEPTH` (mars-ceiling
      §2.2); `channel_incision` is d, unscaled (F2).
    - Wet now: the steady state with the climate's runoff (behind `cfg(test)` until T14.d), ice
      cells shedding it as it stands (Q5), the sea's cells bounds (T14.d adds the lakes by their
      balance), then the remap (_The fixes after T14.c_).
    - Outputs: a fresh routing of the final field (flow, drainage, k_s on the filled surface), both
      runoffs, `channel_incision` and `routed`; no own runoff inside waiting rims or on renewed or
      partly exposed cells; the catchment runoff over the final routing (Q7).
    - The tests: (A) is (A0) recorded, (A1) asserted, (A2) recorded (F1); (B) takes a 10 km valley

      Williams and Phillips 2001: 2,040 ± 1,548 m), then the closure, asserted at the area p99

      mars-ceiling §4.1): (1) a young surface untouched; (2a)–(2b), T14.d's; (2c) on the solver's

  - _The fixes after T14.c_ (`7347836a` and `a8a25ee0`; T14.c follow-ups 1–3). The reference Earth's

    construction's area-weighted heights above base (ties by the final preorder, ratified in
    follow-up 3 §2), re-capped at s_c in preorder.

      2 §2): the construction is already an eroded planet's, so the steady state organises the
      drainage, not the distribution, and checks of land hypsometry after erosion read T12.a's
      bands.
    - Asserted at `7347836a`: (i) relief within 6–16 σ_h; (ii) the land's maximum the
      construction's; (iii) every unbound cell with uplift at or above its receiver, held cells
      below theirs counted apart (follow-up 3 §1); each basin's mean, on the solve before the remap.

      field's 2,574 m; the land's maximum above base 8,299.4 m, the construction's, but 10,696 m
      above the sea (a closed basin's base added); 365 links re-capped; the raw peak 13,956 m; above

      takes the construction's z0 at its cumulative midpoint by solid angle. Then, in the final
      routing's preorder and skipping the held cells, z′ ← min(max(z′, w_r), w_r + s_c δ), w_r the
      receiver's final surface (a bound's water surface or ground, else its final height). The

  - _T14.d_ (the batch's last commit; decision-r09-t14-choices Q3, Q6b, Q7, its T14.d follow-up A–G
    and "T14.d lakes"). The reference Earth's figures here were measured before the lakes fix (the
    last item) unless stated; those after the review's fixes and the first merge are in _The
    reference Earth after the fixes_.
    - _The order_ (Q7; follow-up D). `run` is the solve with provisional outputs, then
      `outputs::finish`: one `match_sigma_h` (the re-match); every cell dried, its water surface to
      its ground and its liquid entry none; `sea::place`; on a world wet now Q3's lakes
      (`Measure::Balance` on the final ground outside the ocean, of the main liquid);
      `reapply_after_erosion`; the final routing and outputs; then `routed`. The figures are written
      at the step's end only where no crater waits; otherwise `after_late_craters` writes them. On a
      world dry now the provisional routing takes every closed depression as a dry playa, not the
      paleo-lakes, so the records the re-match books route as the final field will: routed with the
      paleo-lakes, the reference Mars's σ_h missed by 3.207 × 10⁻³.
    - _Q3's balance in the solve._ The wet-now solve holds the construction's lakes by their water
      balance (`WaterBalance::of`): each cell's inflow its own runoff times its area, its loss
      `NetLoss::at`, E − P at its water surface; each lake bed a bound, each lake's or dry playa's
      level its basin's base level; no lake on a world with no main liquid. Since the review (M1,
      the science check's must-fix) each cell's net loss is (E − P) + r, r its own runoff: E − P
      alone counted a lake's precipitation twice. That is decision-r09-t14-choices Q3's X ratio,
      after Matsubara, Howard and Drummond 2011: X = (E − P) ÷ the runoff from the land outside the
      lake. A new test holds A_L ÷ (A_B − A_L) = runoff ÷ (E − P), measured 0.2003 against 0.2000.
      One balance costs 0.37 s on the level-8 Earth. The bounds after "T14.d lakes" are in the last
      item.
    - _σ_h_ (follow-up C). One re-match: the ruled predicted-record iteration is skipped (main,
      under the owner's FEATURES FIRST of 2026-10-20). The re-match books the channels' share C_c
      from the field routed before the late craters, which `route_final` re-routes. On the reference
      Mars C_c is 108,176 m² at the match, 107,375 m² at the step's end and 111,126 m² after the
      late craters, so the whole pass realises σ_h 1.754 × 10⁻⁴ above plan 14's. That is past the
      fallback's 10⁻⁴, so it went to main first;
      `the_reference_mars_s_whole_pass_realises_its_sigma_h` asserts it at 2 × 10⁻⁴
      (`MARS_WHOLE_PASS_SIGMA_H_TOLERANCE`), and the gap is a finding. The whole-surface test (Mars
      5.1 × 10⁻¹⁵, Moon −9.8 × 10⁻¹⁵, Ceres −4.4 × 10⁻¹⁶) and the late-crater test (2.4 × 10⁻¹⁵)
      hold T12.e's 10⁻⁶. Recorded before the review: the reference Earth −2.23 × 10⁻⁵, the small
      Earth +6.15 × 10⁻⁶. After the review's fixes and the first merge the small Earth's +4.871 ×
      10⁻⁵ and the reference Earth's −2.764 × 10⁻⁵ are each asserted at 10⁻⁴ relative
      (`WET_NOW_SIGMA_H_TOLERANCE`, the review's plan conformance), and the reference Mars's is
      still +1.754 × 10⁻⁴; after the second merge the small Earth +1.910 × 10⁻⁵, the reference Earth
      −4.580 × 10⁻⁵ and the reference Mars +1.754 × 10⁻⁴. On a world wet now the re-match
      books the provisional records, which the new sea, the lakes and the final routing re-route.
    - _The climate_ (Q6b; follow-ups E and G). `ClimateRecords { model: Normalised }` is stored in
      `Working::climate_records` by `finish`: about 2.07 MB on the Earth's 72 × 72 grid (259,200
      values after the second merge, its own records gaining the ocean's heat `ocean_w_m2`; 1.58 MB
      before), 8.5 KB on the radiative model. `reapply_after_erosion` re-writes each climate cell
      from the stored
      records (`write_climate`), re-solves the arithmetic models' constant c′ against the final
      water surfaces and ℓ, applies `floor_climate`, recomputes `cell_temperatures`, then runs
      `place_ices` and `place_liquids`; neither the model nor the hydrology runs again. At unchanged
      heights it reproduces the state to the bit. `NetLoss::{new, at}` is Q3's E − P: E the
      Priestley–Taylor evaporation of the condensable's own open liquid, rebuilt from
      `evaporation`'s parts and the stored records (equal to `hydrology::Evaporation::rates` to the
      bit over 52,344 sea cell-months; after the merges it follows the sea's evaporation as
      R09.T13.i's climate now computes it, still to the bit), none where it is frozen; P the climate
      cell's annual precipitation. The cell's ice share is not applied (labelled). The net loss is
      taken at each cell's water surface, its ground where dry, not at the lake's level, which is
      not known before the fill: an error of Γ times the lake's depth, under a kelvin on the coarse
      cells (labelled).
    - _`reflood` and `route_final`_ (follow-ups B and C; Q7's addition). `sea::reflood` keeps only
      the lakes, cells under liquid whose surface is not ℓ to the bit. `route_final` runs in
      `after_late_craters` between `reflood` and `book`, only where `routed` is set: every cell
      under liquid a seed at its water surface, every dry closed depression a dry playa, the own
      runoffs kept. A world the step does not route keeps every cell `Terminal`. `route_final` and
      `after_late_craters` carry Q7's label since the review: "a paleo-valley beheaded by a late
      crater takes the present drainage downstream, which is smaller than the drainage that cut it".
    - _The outputs_ (Q7). The catchment runoff is the accumulation of own runoff over the field's
      final routing, so the plan's "the solver's equivalent area times 1 m a⁻¹" is restated to that
      accumulation.
    - _The tests._ The small Earth's surface mean T_in is 288.000000000 K after the whole pass, to
      10⁻⁹, and its lakes are level. The catchment flux over the final routing is within 0.0295 of
      its codes on the small Earth's 6,144 cells and the reference Mars's 98,304, against one code's
      half-step of 0.0293, inside the tolerance of the two codes' steps. k_s × A^−θ is the slope to
      the receiver within the steepness code's step (0.0443 at 1,565 cells, 0.0444 at 90,425). On
      the reference Mars every eroded cell's own runoff is 0.1 m a⁻¹; the 52,118 cells whose
      catchments are wholly old take a catchment runoff of 0.1 m a⁻¹; its 44,074 young cells have
      none, and a surface aged 3.5 Ga has none. Q4's (2a) holds under `Rule::Whole` at s\* 0.99341
      over 81 waiting craters, and (2b) to the bit. `route_final` leaves every cell at or above its
      receiver (2,509 flows changed by the late craters) and is idempotent; with no erosion the
      re-match books C_c = 0; the reference Moon and Ceres, at pressure 0, carry no runoff
      (R09.T8.d's invariant). On the reference Earth 1,160 cells carry a catchment runoff at least
      three times their own (at most 49.5 times).

    - _The bench_ `coarse/erosion_l8` (criterion, `iter_batched`, 10 samples;
      `required-features = ["testing"]`): 10.504 s (10.488–10.520 s) per `erosion::run` on the

    - _The lakes fix_ ("T14.d lakes", a blocker). Q3's balance lakes covered 14.1% of the reference
      Earth's land, about 21 × 10⁶ km², against Verpoorter et al. 2014's about 3.7%: 3,231 of its
      4,880 water bodies were full, and the solve kept their beds as bounds, so T12's depressions

      on the final field runs as built, and the dry-now branch is unchanged. Recorded, not asserted,

      terminal and 705 full lakes, 828 playas and 987 held pits; 7.04% after the first merge and M1,

      1,338 held pits (1,317 under a lake, 5 a playa's floor, 6 draining into a lake, 1 to a playa,
      9 to the sea), the links into held pits still 3, and the small Earth 6.38%; a lake candidate

      land's area-weighted quantiles stay within 2 m of the

      of nonglaciated land for lakes above 0.002 km², and the cells of about 1,300 km² resolve only

    its batch 2 (the sea's evaporation) and R09.T8.d. `NetLoss` follows the sea's evaporation as the

  - _A channel-initiation area._ One sourced and independent of the grid, so that a cell carries a
    valley and the closure only above it, is a later item, with no owner until a source exists
    (main's ruling); without it level 8's dependence on resolution stands, and a larger world dry
    now at level 8 draws twice the density. T6.c's closure narrows it: the reference Mars at level
    8 (cells of about 19 km; rule 4's slow run, `the_reference_mars_s_slow_record`, 2026-10-22)
    gives (B)'s p99 0.978 of its bound (175.3 m against 182 m) and (A2) 3.06 m, against level 7's
    0.826 and 1.96 m, where T14's trunk closure gave 1.94 times and 5.64 m. Its (A1) trunk median

    and Phillips 2001's depths, p90 412.3 m, maximum 2,435.5 m. So the drawn valleys show T14's

  - _Files and public items._

      `NONE_RETAINED`, `new`, `get`, `from_density`, `density`). `cells.rs`'s documentation of
      `SurfaceClass` and `crater_state`; one line of `material/classify.rs`'s documentation.
      `wire/tests.rs`'s codes writer appends the 39 assigned class codes and the crater state's
      256 values: `tests/golden/wire/codes.golden` gains 295 lines, its range lines and header
      unchanged.
    - The sim: `steps/classes.rs` (`run`, the step), the private `steps/classes/koppen.rs` (the
      table, `classify` over a `Year` of its figures) and `steps/classes/tests.rs`;
      `quantise::header_pressure` now `pub(crate)`, the step reading the header's pressure; the
      module documentation of `surface/mod.rs` and `steps/mod.rs`, and two test helpers' notes in
      `steps/erosion/`; `examples/surface_map.rs` with its `[[example]]` entry (the sim's first).
  - _The crater state's byte stays a `u8`._ `SynthesisCell::crater_state` keeps its type, its codes
    `CraterState`'s, so that no layout, wire table or fixture moves (§6 asks for the newtype, not a
    field of that type; the Rust review's "consider" to type the field, declined for that reason).
  - _The months' shares from their edges._ Each month counts as its `month_edges` span over 2π, on
    the seasonal orbit's eccentricity (the header's `season_eccentricity`), not by `month_share`,
    which reads a header the pass has not built (T2's note on `month_edges`); the shares are the
    same.
  - _The summer on the climate cell's anomalies._ The warmest window is chosen on the months'
    anomalies, so that it is the climate cell's alone, whatever a field cell's height (§4's "the
    choice is the climate cell's"; the plan-conformance review). The classifier's months carry
    their anomalies, the annual mean apart.
  - _The crater state's own rounding._ `CraterState::from_density` rounds 8 log₂ N and holds the
    code to 2–255 itself, not through `log_code`, which refuses codes above its maximum and gives 0
    below code 1, where §6 holds and code 1 means none retained.
  - _The organic cover, read twice._ `steps::classes::organic_cover` repeats R10's rule (the first
    `Cover` entry of the organic family), `organic_cover_entry` being crate-private in the surface
    crate.
  - _The golden's names._ `codes.golden` names the crater state's values `crater_state_km2[c]`, in
    km⁻², for §7(c)'s `crater_state[c]`.
  - _One chord._ The rim test reads the craters' own `chord_m`, which `each_lift` now calls too (the
    determinism review), its arithmetic unchanged; and the sea's surface is compared with ℓ with
    either zero's sign folded, so that a −0 can never make a sea a lake.
  - _The example's directory._ `surface_map` takes an optional output directory; the default is
    the workspace's `target/surface_map/`.
  - _Whole months count whole._ On a circular orbit the month shares are twelfths only to rounding,
    so four of them summed to 3.999… and missed b's four-month threshold. A count within 10⁻⁹
    twelfths (about 0.03 s of an Earth year) of its threshold meets it (`COUNT_TOLERANCE_TWELFTHS`).
  - _The small Earth's classes ride an existing pass._ Its whole pass takes 108 s alone at load
    about 7, so its pass-level checks (every cell classified, Köppen–Geiger on land, the liquid
    forms on water, none retained under water, every world's cells classified with a crater state)
    joined `planetary::surface`'s `the_pass_yields_a_valid_field_twice_with_identical_bytes`, which
    already runs it twice; `steps::classes`'s lifeless test is hand-built on the small Earth's grid.

- **Main's rulings on R09.T16's cost findings** (decision-r09-pass-cost, 2026-10-23). None is a
  blocker under the owner's rule of 2026-10-20, and T16 lands as built.
  - _The 94.9 s pass breaks no contract._ It runs as one bulk job on the pool, off the runtime,
    shared by one flight and kept in the field cache. `surface_field` waits for it, but the
    terrain's store asks through the link's own request client, which has no timer. The client's
    `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` of 30 s belongs to `useServerRequest`, for the displays' requests, and
    the server sets no deadline. Meanwhile the body has no coverage, so it stays on R07's disc
    (R10.T10.e) with `SURVEY COVERAGE: PENDING` (R10.T12): a stated wait, not a wrong picture.
    At version 23 no generated body runs a pass (the serve gate is shut until 24). The
    brainstorm's "tens of seconds" and decision-r09-t14-choices C's 60 s are recorded references,
    both missed; C's 60 s guarded the σ_h iteration, whose fallback T14.d took.
  - _The climate step's 68.9 s is not R09.T13.i's G runs._ Those are inside the 31.8 s quiet at
    which T13.i landed, and seed 3's 64–73 s is another world's, measured before the change below.
    Both steps rose between `01674b8c` (T14.d) and `898a3c94` (this task's base): the climate
    from 31.8 to 68.9 s, and the erosion from 10.50 to 17.88 s, though it runs no G run. In that
    range only P14.T54.a's 22 → 23 batch touches the climate's code or the reference worlds'
    inputs (R09.T6.c's change to the erosion is its dry-now branch, and other plan 14 commits
    change only the registry that the climate reads). The batch's phase-data switch (`032a8c5f`)
    makes every saturation pressure T49.b's curve: water's six `libm::pow`, an `ln` and an `exp`
    a call, where the held curve took one `exp`. The erosion's two water balances make up to
    some 28 million such calls a pass, which fits its rise. The energy balance reads its water
    terms from tables, so the climate's rise is not attributed. It is a cost of ruled physics,
    measured late: not a bug and not a ruled cost. R09.T16.a attributes it. P14.T53.a is not part
    of it: it is not in this task's tree, and at version 23 `GreenhouseConstants::in_force` gives
    the held constants, once a body.
  - _A pass's 408 MB_ (the process's peak, its 22 MB floor included) is no crash risk at the
    passes the client asks for, the bodies near a view's camera (one or two). Fifteen at once is
    not reachable today. R09.T17.a bounds the passes in flight, which also keeps a pool worker
    free for the displays' requests.
  - _The fast order test's 909.5 s and the bytes test's 248.7 s_ stay in the fast tier as built,
    unsplit and uncut. decision-p14-t54a-passes §C.7's pre-authorised split excludes determinism
    and order tests, and decision-r09-t13-test-cost keeps their coverage first. The cost stays
    I13's. R09.T16.a times both on a quiet machine.
